content:
Alice Nguyen: FYI customer cust-8345 opened a ticket — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~340ms to ~1.1s after last night's quant-profile deployment (quant-profile-v2). They saw several 504s when batch=8.
Samir Patel: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the exact model id? Only this customer or global?
Alice Nguyen: Repro request from their workload (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-neo-13b-quant-int8-v2","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":8}'
```
They say it was fine before 2026-03-12T03:40Z when quant-profile-v2 rolled.
Maria Gomez: I pulled the perf traces from canary and ran an offline calibration repro. Observations: for several prompt distributions the quant kernels hit outlier ranges and we fall back to slower FP-paths. Calibration stats (excerpt):
```
[calib-run] samples=32k, outlier_pct=12.8%, KL_tail>threshold=15.2%
[quantize] observed inf/NaN during fp8-accum in 0.3% of forward passes -> fallback path triggered
```
This explains the p99 tail — a small number of sequences cause expensive kernel fallback.
Lee Chen: Runtime change note: we recently enabled contiguous-batching heuristics that increase average batch length; combined with the quantization kernel selector, it can push some batches into slower codegen paths when fallback happens. Two immediate mitigations: enable model-level fallback-to-fp16 variant for the customer OR route their traffic to Dedicated capacity (isolates scheduling noise). Also we can flip a flag `quant.fallback=true` on the model so fallback is allowed earlier (avoids repeated kernel switching hits).
Samir Patel: For a hotfix I'd prefer routing them to an fp16-fallback variant while we investigate calibration. Plan:
- Create fp16-fallback variant (keeps same weights, runs on fp16 kernels).
- Canary route 5% of their traffic to fp16-fallback for 15m and measure p95/p99.
I opened rollout RB-5432. ETA ~30m to have variant live.
Maria Gomez: Longer-term fix: re-run calibration with broader prompt sampling (increase `calib_samples` 20k -> 100k) and increase outlier clipping threshold, then produce a new quant-profile-v2a. That reduced NaN-induced fallbacks in my local repro before.
Lee Chen: I'm applying the temporary routing + enabling `quant.fallback=true` for cust-8345 now. Command I used: 
```json
POST /admin/routing/policies
{
  "customer_id": "cust-8345",
  "route_rules": [{"percent":95,"variant":"redwood-neo-13b-quant-int8-v2"},{"percent":5,"variant":"redwood-neo-13b-fp16-fallback"}]
}
```
deploy-bot: route update applied (policy id rp-8791) :white_check_mark:
Alice Nguyen: I notified the customer of the temporary change and asked them to run their workload for 30m and report any regressions. Monitoring: baseline p95=120ms p99=340ms, post-quant p95=160ms p99=1.08s. Target for hotfix p99 < 400ms.
Samir Patel: Next actions assigned: Samir -> rollback plan if fp16-fallback shows regressions; Maria -> kick off re-calibration job (calib_samples=100k) and produce new quant-profile; Lee -> monitor routing metrics and increase canary if stable. I'll update RB-5432 with results. :thumbsup:
Alice Nguyen: Thanks team. I'll keep ticket open and paste graphs here after 15m.
deploy-bot: metric alert cleared for cust-8345 p99 spike after routing (at 2470016200).
Alice Nguyen: Customer confirmed reduced latency on their side, no more 504s. Closing provisional mitigation; leaving tasks for re-calibration and profile re-release.
